## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Follow-up on head `a47f2b7`, reassessing the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13038#issuecomment-5806344687) of `9d414d9`. Both earlier findings about the unchanged-color shortcut are resolved. The rewritten `test/shell.d/theme-set-browser-test.sh` now fails on Linux when run as a normal user, and it can refresh the developer's running browsers.

**Verified** at `a47f2b7` (stubbed writer, `sudo`/`pkexec`, `pgrep` and browsers; private policy directories):

| Earlier finding | Status |
|---|---|
| `browser-policy-sudoers-test.sh` depends on the host's policy files | **Resolved.** The test points the new `OMARCHY_BROWSER_POLICY_DIRS` override at a private `#ff0000` fixture that no case expects. It passes as a normal user, as simulated root and with `stat -c` unavailable. |
| Shortcut keeps `color.json` files the writer would have normalized | **Resolved on Linux.** A canonical root:root 0644 file skips the writer. A different `BrowserColorScheme`, a symlink, mode 0664 or 0600, or a user-owned file each call the writer. |
| Optional test improvement (grep-only test) | Partly addressed, see below. |
| Description note | Unchanged, see below. |

### New `theme-set-browser-test.sh` fails for a normal Linux user

The first case writes a matching `color.json` owned by whoever runs the test and expects the setter to skip the writer. `file_is_canonical` requires `root:root 644` whenever `stat -c` works, so on Linux the writer is called and the test stops at its first assertion. The later cases never run.

| Runner | Result |
|---|---|
| Linux, normal user | **fail**: `not ok - setter skipped the privileged write when color.json already matches` |
| Linux, simulated root (user namespace) | pass |
| `stat -c` unavailable (emulated BSD `stat`) | pass |
| Linux, normal user, setter ownership check removed (diagnostic copy) | pass |

**Impact:** The shell suite reports this file as failed on a Linux developer machine. This is a test-only failure. The production shortcut behaves as intended.

**Suggested change:** Let the test control the ownership result, for example with a `stat` stub in `$TMP_BIN` that reports `root:root 644` for the matching case. Add negative cases for a non-root owner or mode 0664, a different `BrowserColorScheme` and a symlink. Removing the ownership, content or symlink check from the setter currently leaves the test passing, so these cases would also cover the new hardening.

### New test can refresh the developer's running browsers

The test stubs only `omarchy-theme-set-browser-policy`. The real `omarchy-cmd-present`, `pgrep` and browser commands stay on `PATH`, so every case that reaches the writer also runs the refresh block. For each installed and running Chromium-family browser, it executes `<browser> --refresh-platform-policy --no-startup-window`. With `pgrep` stubbed to report browsers running, one refresh call per browser command was logged.

**Impact:** Running the shell suite reloads policy in the developer's open browsers. `docs/testing.md` asks tests to stub helpers so they run without touching the developer's machine. The effect is limited to a policy reload.

**Suggested change:** Stub `omarchy-cmd-present` to exit 1 in `$TMP_BIN`, as `browser-policy-sudoers-test.sh` already does.

**Optional test improvement:** The skip, mismatch and no-directory cases are now behavioral tests, and disabling the skip or reverting the `saw_any` guard fails them. Several other mutations still pass:
- all refresh `&` removed, so refreshes run serially again;
- the preload line commented out;
- the preload `&` removed.

The reviewed-head check `grep -qE 'omarchy-theme-switcher --preload.*&$'` caught the last case and was removed in this commit. Also, `grep -q 'pids=\(\)'` is a basic regular expression with an empty group, so it matches any `pids=`. Restoring the preload check and using `grep -qF 'pids=()'` would close these gaps.

**Description note:** The PR body's Tested section still says the test checks that `omarchy-theme-set` backgrounds the preload, but this commit removed that check. The earlier description note still applies: refreshing only running browsers predates this PR, and the skip applies when the same color is reapplied, not when switching between stock themes.

**No-directory guard** (raised in a [separate comment](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13038#issuecomment-5806534437)): With no managed directory, `$saw_any && $all_unchanged && exit 0` now calls the writer, as the base did. The writer only writes into existing directories and never creates one, so this call writes nothing. The browser install and migration paths create the directory before calling the setter, so a first theme apply writes policies either way. The guard is defensive and does not change first-apply behavior.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of head `a47f2b7` against `9d414d9` and base `d3cfd53`, plus sandboxed runs of both changed tests, targeted mutations and the setter directly, with the privileged writer, `sudo`/`pkexec`, `pgrep` and browsers stubbed and private policy directories. Root ownership was simulated with a user namespace, and non-GNU `stat` with a shim. No real root account, macOS host, real browser or real `/etc` policy directory was used. A root-owned file with a non-root group was checked from source only. Timings were not re-measured.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments of this follow-up, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
